newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end lower as ADRs slide on Wall St.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end lower as ADRs slide on Wall St.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed lower for the first time in four sessions Thursday after dealers booked profits amid a slide by Mexican ADRs on Wall Street.
"The last few days' gains were just on in-and-out trading and a few attractive stocks, so profit-taking was logical," said Jaime Fernandez, an equity analyst at the Interacciones brokerage.
The leading IPC share index ended down 36.10 points, or 0.94 percent, at 3,798.37. Trading volume was moderate at 62.2 million shares.
"Furthermore, volatility on the Dow Jones (Industrial Average) and the outlook for (first-quarter earnings) reports also took its toll," Fernandez said. The Dow closed 21.27 points lower at 6,658.60.
Activity was slower than usual because of a dearth of foreign investors in the market, traders said.
"Traders did nothing. Maybe they are taking a breather before stepping back in to buy," a floor trader said.
Declines by the American Depositary Receipts of Telmex and Televisa weighed the most on the market, traders said.
Telecomms firm Telmex declined 3/8 to 41-7/8 on Wall Street, while media group Televisa was off 1/8 to 26-1/4.
Telmex L shares meanwhile closed unchanged at 16.58 pesos ($2.10), while Televisa CPO shares were off 1.40 pesos (18 cents) at 102.60 pesos ($13.02).
Dealers said Televisa shares were hit in early trade by shock news former long-serving company chief Emilio Azcarraga Milmo had died.
Nonetheless, they said the news was softened because a new management line-up had been in place since March 4.
A total of 117 stocks changed hands on the broad market, of which decliners outnumbered gainers by 58 to 31.
